newsitem.title: CHINA: China rubber imports seen high, prices to drop.
newsitem.headline: China rubber imports seen high, prices to drop.

text.p: China's rubber market is likely to continue to see oversupply this year although imports will remain high despite a possible small decline, the China Daily said on Wednesday.
Rubber supply surged 22.6 percent to 1.89 million tonnes last year, compared with 1.46 million tonnes in 1995, it said. Total consumption grew 7.0 percent to 1.4 million tonnes last year.
"The glut of rubber will add to this year's rubber supply," it quoted Chen Guoying, secretary-general of the Chinese Rubber Industry Association as saying.
China produced 973,000 tonnes of rubber last year, with synthetic rubber accounting for 56 percent, the newspaper said.
Domestic rubber demand was seen increasing by 5.0 percent to 1.47 million tonnes this year, with domestic output seen at 1.05 million tonnes.
"The import of rubber... will see a slight decline because of last year's inventory," Chen said.
Imports acccounted for about half of annual consumption. Imports hit 917,000 tonnes last year, soaring 45.1 percent from 1995. Natural rubber imports jumped 72.1 percent to 550,000 tonnes.

"The price decline in the international rubber market partly resulted in the surge in imports last year," the newspaper quoted Zhao Wenquan, deputy director of the rubber division under the Ministry of Chemical Industry, as saying.
Oversupply of rubber last year sent domestic prices plunging to about 13,000 yuan ($1,566) per tonne, down from a record high of 18,000 per tonne in the previous two years,.
"This year's price is likely to continue decreasing, but at the same pace as last year," Chen said.
The lower price failed to boost tyre production because of stockpiles resulting from a stagnant car market, the newspaper said.
Total tyre production last year was estimated at 61 million, with unsold stock surging 20 percent from 1995.
